saints.name: St. Meletius of Antioch
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: A gentle bishop of Antioch, thrice driven into exile for the Nicene faith, who presided over the First Council of Constantinople…
biography: Meletius, previously bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, was made bishop of Antioch in 360, when Arians and orthodox alike hoped to claim him. Barely a month after his enthronement he preached on the words of Proverbs, 'The Lord created me in the beginning of his ways,' confessing the divinity of the Son, and the Emperor Constantius II banished him — the first of three exiles under Arian emperors.

Restored at last in 378, he found his flock divided by schism, the orthodox Paulinus holding a rival claim to the see. Gentle and beloved, he ordained the young John Chrysostom to his first office in the church, and Chrysostom later preached his praises.

In 381 he presided over the First Council of Constantinople, the second ecumenical council, and enthroned Gregory of Nazianzus as bishop of the capital. While the council still sat he died, mourned by the whole assembly; Gregory of Nyssa preached his funeral oration, and his body was carried back to Antioch.
saints.knownFor: Presiding over the First Council of Constantinople in 381.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 12 February
